text: Product walkthrough Sounding: an AI meeting notetaker, built like Fathom Record → speaker-labelled transcript → notes, action items, clips and search. For one person, and for a team. Open models on one GPU: Parakeet (speech), Sortformer + TitaNet (who spoke), Qwen (notes) The capture layer is stubbed on purpose: you upload the recording instead of a bot joining the call Seeded with real recorded meetings, including hour-long calls with 8–9 people
Anyone can open the live app. Reviewers get in with one click, with no account to create.
The meetings list. Every title, meeting type, summary line and action-item count was produced by the pipeline from real recordings.
The case that matters: a real hour-long research meeting with eight people (ICSI corpus).
The first speaker model could only track 4 people. I measured against human labels and added voice-embedding clustering: speaker mix-ups fell from ~20% to ~6%.
Press play and the transcript follows. Click any line to jump the recording to that moment.
The notes. An hour is too long to read, so every point links to the moment it came from. Invented timestamps are thrown away.
Switch the template and the notes are rewritten for that kind of meeting: here, a sales discovery (SPICED) layout.
While Qwen rewrites the notes in the background, the action items: each one has the speaker, the moment, and an owner you can assign.
Assigning someone sends them a notification with a link to the moment.
Ask a question about this meeting. The answer cites the moments it used.
Qwen reads the whole hour-long transcript (32k-token context)…
Timestamps in the answer are buttons that jump the recording there.
Hear something worth keeping? Highlight saves the last 20 seconds and the next 10, because by the time you react, the moment has passed.
You can also clip any range from the transcript: line menu → "Clip from here" → "End clip here".
Share the clip with someone who was not on the call: one public link, for that clip only.
To prove it, log out completely…
…and open the link. The clip plays with its own transcript. The rest of the recording is not exposed.
Search runs across every transcript and every set of notes you can see, and results open at the exact moment.
Ask Sounding answers across all your calls, citing the meeting and the moment.
Keyword retrieval (BM25) picks the relevant excerpts from 9 meetings, then Qwen answers…
Each citation links to the meeting and the moment.
Trackers flag moments across every call. Keyword trackers match words; AI trackers match meaning, so "we need it by Friday" counts as a deadline.
Coaching: talk time, questions and monologues per person, plus AI scorecards for each meeting type, with evidence.
Playlists collect clips across meetings. "Play all" runs them back to back, which is useful for onboarding or a decision review.
Companies are grouped from attendee email domains. Folders and sharing controls (private, team, organization, links) complete the team side.
New recordings come in by upload. This is the stub where Fathom's bot would join the call. The pipeline after it is the same.
Processing: preparing audio → finding speakers → transcribing → writing notes → running trackers.
Meanwhile, the admin side: teams and roles, invite links, meeting types (detected automatically), custom templates, scorecards and a transcription dictionary.
Back to the upload…
Done. The meeting was titled, split by speaker, transcribed and summarised in about a minute.

What's built, and what I left out Built for the hour-long, eight-person call Built: transcripts, cited notes, templates, action items, clips and playlists, sharing and links, comments, search, Ask across calls, trackers, coaching, scorecards, teams and admin, API and webhooks Stubbed: calendar sync and the meeting bot (uploads go through the same pipeline) Left out: email, CRM sync, SSO. Next: a Google Meet bot, then live notes during the call Code and agent logs are in the repo · live at http://5.9.117.80:3000
